findings.source_passage: And have I not tallied the whale, Ahab would mutter to himself, as after poring over his charts till long after midnight he would throw himself back in reveries—tallied him, and shall he escape?
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical self-interrogation 'tallied him, and shall he escape?' is the signature moment of Ahab's monomania made vocal; collapsing it to 'I have tallied him' strips the voice entirely and eliminates the dramatic self-address that critics fix on.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the verbatim interior monologue: 'have I not tallied the whale … tallied him, and shall he escape?' The exact phrasing is the point.

findings.source_passage: when this hell in himself yawned beneath him, a wild cry would be heard through the ship; and with glaring eyes Ahab would burst from his state room, as though escaping from a bed that was on fire.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Often, when forced from his hammock'
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence 'as though escaping from a bed that was on fire' is a defining image of Ahab's psychological state and widely noted in criticism; the draft's 'burst from his room as from a burning bed' reduces it to a bare simile, erasing Melville's specific cumulative rhetoric.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the full sentence rhythm and the simile 'as though escaping from a bed that was on fire' verbatim rather than compressing.

findings.source_passage: the mind does not exist unless leagued with the soul, therefore it must have been that, in Ahab's case, yielding up all his thoughts and fancies to his one supreme purpose; that purpose, by its own sheer inveteracy of will, forced itself against gods and devils into a kind of self-assumed, independent being of its own.
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, philosophical explanation of Ahab's dissociation
findings.why_it_matters: This is the interpretive crux of the chapter—the argument that Ahab's purpose has become a separate, autonomous being—and the specific language 'forced itself against gods and devils' and 'self-assumed, independent being of its own' is essential to the metaphysical argument critics return to. The draft shortens it to 'assumed a sort of self-subsistent being,' losing 'against gods and devils' entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'forced itself against gods and devils into a kind of self-assumed, independent being of its own' verbatim; this is doctrine, not ornament.

findings.source_passage: Nay, could grimly live and burn, while the common vitality to which it was conjoined, fled horror-stricken from the unbidden and unfathered birth.
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, after 'self-assumed, independent being of its own'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Unbidden and unfathered birth' is a distinctive and interpretively loaded phrase—the monomania as an illegitimate autonomous creation—and it is simply missing from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert 'Nay, could grimly live and burn, while the common vitality … fled horror-stricken from the unbidden and unfathered birth' before the somnambulistic passage.

findings.source_passage: sperm whales, guided by some infallible instinct—say, rather, secret intelligence from the Deity—mostly swim in veins
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Besides, when making a passage'
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical 'say, rather, secret intelligence from the Deity' is a characteristic Melvillean voice-register moment—ironic, theological, digressive—and its omission flattens the whale-vein passage to plain natural history.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'say, rather, secret intelligence from the Deity' as an inline parenthetical when introducing whale veins.

findings.source_passage: carried them on amid a clashing of phrensies, and whirled them round and round and round in his blazing brain, till the very throbbing of his life-spot became insufferable anguish
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Often, when forced from his hammock'
findings.why_it_matters: The triple 'round and round and round' and 'throbbing of his life-spot' are prosodically distinctive and establish the fever-pitch register of Ahab's nocturnal torment; the draft compresses to 'whirled them,' losing the incantatory rhythm and the unique phrase 'life-spot.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'whirled them round and round and round in his blazing brain, till the very throbbing of his life-spot became insufferable anguish' as close to verbatim as the word budget allows.

summary: Multiple high-severity losses—the 'tallied him, and shall he escape?' self-interrogation flattened, 'as though escaping from a bed that was on fire' compressed away, and the crucial 'forced itself against gods and devils into a kind of self-assumed, independent being' passage gutted—plus several medium-severity voice erasures make this draft unacceptable without a regeneration pass.
